title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week

    . This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Positive

While no major changes have emerged in recent sessions, several subtle shifts are developing beneath the surface. Large and mid-cap indices continue to trade above their rising 10- and 20-day moving averages and are holding above their 50-day MAs, maintaining a constructive price and trend structure. Small caps, however, are lagging slightly, still trading below their 50-day MA and struggling to keep pace.

Market internals remain broadly positive. Breadth—measured by new highs versus new lows—and momentum—tracked via up versus down volume—continue to show favorable readings. That said, the strong upside skew seen earlier (e.g., 3-to-1 in favor of new highs and positive momentum) has now moderated toward parity. This moderation typically precedes a period of chop or short-term consolidation as buying pressure fades.

On the sector front, there’s been visible rotation. Technology, which recently surged from the bottom to the top of the sector rankings, has now settled into the middle of the pack. Energy and Healthcare sectors have begun to roll over after hitting resistance zones, signaling possible sector-wide fatigue. The next few sessions will be critical in assessing whether other sectors follow suit and how the rankings evolve during a potential pullback or digestion phase.

Risk Management and Exposure Control

  • Maintain a Cautiously Bullish Stance: Major indices continue to hold above rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, but recent momentum has slowed. Maintain a positive bias, but stay nimble in case of short-term consolidation.

  • Scale Exposure Selectively: Favor continued gradual scaling into high-quality setups. Focus on technical confirmation before increasing position sizes.

  • Manage Underperformers Actively: Reduce or exit positions that fail to keep pace with the broader market or show weakness near resistance zones. Rotate into names maintaining relative strength.

Market Monitoring and Internal Indicators

  • Track Trend Continuity: Higher lows and improving moving average slopes remain constructive. Monitor whether large, mid, and small caps can continue holding above the 50-day MAs.

  • Watch for Internal Deceleration: Breadth and momentum are still positive but have moderated. A move from strong breadth skew to near-parity often signals a digestion phase.

  • Identify Warning Signs Early: A breakdown in breadth or a narrowing of advancing stocks without corresponding price weakness may hint at underlying fatigue.

Sector and Theme Development

  • Growth Sector Watchlist: Technology has pulled back from recent leadership but remains structurally intact. Monitor for resumed strength in tech, discretionary, and semis.

  • Rotation Signals Emerging: Defensive sectors are slipping in rank. Healthcare and energy have shown weakness after hitting resistance. Use this as a guide for reallocation if the trend continues.

  • Evaluate Emerging Themes: Look for strength in under-the-radar sectors or stocks forming new bases amid the rotation.

Capital Allocation and Trade Execution

  • Prioritize Setup Quality Over Quantity: Look for stocks with:

    • Clean consolidation patterns

    • Breakouts with volume confirmation

    • Constructive pullbacks to rising MAs

  • Stick to Defined Risk Parameters: Place stops just below recent swing lows or MA support. Avoid oversized positions, especially in names near resistance or in lagging sectors.

  • Avoid Overexposure in Fading Momentum: Keep cash levels flexible as conditions may slow before a next leg higher or rotate internally.

Daily Reassessment and Adaptive Strategy

  • Test of Support May Be Imminent: If indices pause or pull back, watch whether rising 10/20-day MAs hold. That would reinforce market health.

  • Let Internal Conditions Drive Exposure:

    • If breadth and price continue expanding: Increase exposure in top setups.

    • If internals weaken or indices falter at key levels: Decrease exposure and raise cash.

Key Focus Areas

  • Be Patient with Entries: Don’t chase breakouts that are extended. Favor pullbacks, flags, and bases near support with clear entry points.

  • Stay Attuned to Setup Quality: Setup expansion has been positive—let that continue to guide your trading decisions more than broad index moves.

  • Remain Flexible: The market may still digest gains through rotation or short-term volatility. Adjust quickly as leadership and internals shift.

Bottom Line

The market has continued to firm up technically, with indices holding above rising key moving averages and internals still broadly supportive. Momentum is slowing, suggesting a possible pause or rotation phase. Use this period to build a watchlist, act on quality setups, and manage risk tightly. The tone remains constructively bullish, but confirmation from growth sectors and broad participation is needed to support more aggressive positioning.
